title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a scheme of characteristic p, and we work on its crystalline site, i.e. with PD-thickenings S' of S. The page treats the easiest case of a Dieudonné theory by crystals for finite group schemes, namely finite étale p-groups. It is the étale analogue of the W-valued Hom construction on the previous page.

(1) Covariant crystal. Let G be finite étale over S, killed by p^n. By topological invariance of the étale site, G lifts uniquely to a finite étale G' on any thickening S', again killed by p^n. Put M_{S'} = G' ⊗_{Z/p^n} O_{S'} = G' ⊗_{Z/p^n} (O_{S'}/p^n). As S' varies these form a crystal D_*(G).

(2) Frobenius. The relative Frobenius f: G → G^{(p)} is an isomorphism because G is étale. Functoriality and base-change compatibility give an isomorphism F_*: D_*(G) → D_*(G^{(p)}) = D_*(G)^{(p)}.

(3) Contravariant version. Use the Pontryagin-type dual Ǧ = Hom_gr(G, (Q_p/Z_p)_S), which is again étale, and set D^*(G) = D_*(Ǧ). This is a contravariant functor with an isomorphism F^*: D^*(G)^{(p)} ≅ D^*(G). V^* is then forced by F^*V^* = p·id, i.e. V^* = p(F^*)^{-1}.

(4) Level-n flat case. Suppose G is flat over Λ_n = Z/p^n, i.e. G is an étale truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level n, locally (Z/p^n)^r. Then D^*(G) is a crystal of locally free Λ_n-modules of finite type whose F is an isomorphism; V is determined uniquely. G ↦ D^*(G) is claimed to be an anti-equivalence onto such 'unit-root' F-crystals over Z/p^n. The margin says 'vérifier'.

(5) General case. Finite étale p-groups are anti-equivalent to F- (or F-V-) crystals that are étale-locally direct sums of the previous type, with varying n.

(6) Recovering G. If G ↔ M, then G(S) ≅ Hom_gr(Λ_{n,S}, G) ≅ Hom_{F-V-cris}(M, O_{S,cris}) ≅ Hom_{F-cris}(…). So G is recovered as F-invariant homomorphisms from its crystal to the structure crystal. This is an Artin–Schreier–Witt / unit-root type description.

Purpose: these are the 'trivial' building blocks (étale, and on the next page multiplicative) for the crystalline Dieudonné functor on finite and Barsotti–Tate groups being developed in this dossier (letter to Tate, May 1966; Montréal 1970 programme). The next page derives the multiplicative case by Cartier duality.
errors: The final formula G(S) ≅ Hom_{F-V-cris}(M, O_{S,cris}) cannot be literally right as written. M is p^n-torsion, so Hom into a p-torsion-free O_cris can vanish; for example, over a perfect field the crystalline structure sheaf is W(k), which is torsion-free. The target should be O_cris/p^n, or O_cris ⊗ Q_p/Z_p, the analogue of W_∞ = lim W_n on the previous page. Then F-invariants give W_n(k^sep)^{σ=1} = Z/p^n, as required.

The anti-equivalence in the level-n case is only asserted, and Grothendieck himself flagged it 'vérifier'. Over a non-reduced S it needs care: one must identify F-crystals whose F is an isomorphism with lisse Z/p^n-étale sheaves. This is a Katz-type argument, not an immediate one.

Minor: in the general case the claim implicitly requires that F-crystals which are étale-locally sums of the flat type have morphisms that also respect the decomposition. This is fine but unproved here.

ideas.what: Crystal attached to a finite étale p-group: G' ⊗ O_{S'} on thickenings, using unique lifting of étale objects.
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné crystal of an étale finite flat group scheme / étale part of crystalline Dieudonné theory
ideas.where_published: Likely implicit in 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970, publ. 1974); worked out in BBM 'Théorie de Dieudonné cristalline II'

ideas.what: Anti-equivalence between étale truncated BT groups of level n (resp. finite étale p-groups) and F-crystals with F an isomorphism (unit-root F-crystals mod p^n).
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root F-crystals ↔ étale Z/p^n- (Z_p-) local systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (1973, 'p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms', Prop. 4.1.1); Crew (1987); classical Artin–Schreier–Witt / Lang torsor argument
ideas.where_published: Not known in Grothendieck's published texts; the standard reference is Katz 1973

ideas.what: Recovering G as F-invariant homomorphisms from its crystal to the structure crystal: G(S) = Hom_F(M, O_cris).
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius-fixed points / Artin–Schreier–Witt description of étale local systems from unit-root crystals

ideas.what: Contravariant D^* defined via the Pontryagin dual Hom(G, Q_p/Z_p), with V^* determined by F^*V^* = p.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, probably between 1966 and the early 1970s, the equivalence between finite étale p-groups (étale truncated BT_n) and unit-root F-crystals over Z/p^n, with recovery of G as F-invariant Homs into the structure crystal. In the literature this is usually attributed to Katz (1973). This is a priority/historical note, not new mathematics.
missed.quote: on obtient une anti-équivalence de la catégorie des G et des F-cristaux précédents ... G(S) ≃ Hom_gr(Λ_{nS}, G) ≃ Hom_{F-V-cris}(M, O_{S,cris})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is history-of-ideas relevance only. It documents that the unit-root/étale correspondence was part of Grothendieck's crystalline Dieudonné programme. The result itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard étale (unit-root) case of crystalline Dieudonné theory and Katz's unit-root correspondence, at finite level. It is mildly interesting as an early Grothendieck formulation, but nothing here is absent from the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: The tensor subscript in M_{S'} is ⊗_{Z/p^n Z}; the image shows a corrected 'Z/p^n Z', with an earlier subscript overwritten.
In 'V^* est uniquement défini par ...' the struck-through text is 'D^*(G)'. The definition continues as 'F^*V^* = p id_{D^*(G)}', i.e. V^* is determined by this relation.
The word under '≃' at the bottom, transcribed 'unpd.', is uncertain. It sits under the first isomorphism and may be an abbreviation such as 'unpd.'/'unip.'; illegible.
The last term is cut off: '≃ Hom_{F-cris}(…', presumably Hom_{F-cris}(M, O_{S,cris}) or a variant.
